summary: Concurrent canary swap caused transcript-merge conflicts, streaming disconnects, and billing amplification for LyceumEDU
description: Issue summary: On 2026-02-18 during a coordinated canary swap of quantized variants for redwood-open-7b-v2, a subset of LyceumEDU traffic experienced merged transcripts (responses that combined text from two distinct requests), abrupt streaming disconnects, and a correlated spike in token billing. Impact: ~12% of Lyceum sessions (enterprise account) showed interleaved transcript fragments, 27% experienced interrupted streaming connections requiring client reconnects, and Lyceum reported a 3.8x unexpected token billing delta during the 18:22–19:05 UTC window. Timeline: 18:10 — Canary rollout started (automated controller kicked off parallel swaps across two clusters). 18:21 — First customer report: partial transcripts with merged segments. 18:25 — SRE observed increased 5xx and stream resets in us-east serving-runtime logs. 18:30 — Immediate rollback of canary group A initiated. 18:33 — Customer escalated to support and requested root-cause. 18:45 — Mitigation: full rollback completed, stream reconnections stabilized by 18:50. 19:05 — Billing exposure window closed; billing team started anomaly investigation. Steps to reproduce: 1) Trigger concurrent canary swap that overlaps routing table updates for session-affinity keys. 2) Route two near-simultaneous requests from same session-id boundary to two different model variants while KV cache warmup is in-progress. 3) Observe token accounting showing double-count for overlapping KV cache initialization and duplicate completion emission. Observed behavior: - Partial transcript merging where completion tokens from request A appear appended into request B and vice versa. - Streaming connection terminated mid-stream with connection reset errors on the runtime (grpc: stream closed by server). - Billing subsystem attributing duplicated tokens for the same session window. Initial mitigation: Immediate canary rollback and temporary enforcement of single-active-canary-per-session placement policy. We also added a temporary routing guard to avoid swapping active session-affinity routes until KV caches stabilize. Logs & traces: - Serving runtime logs: repeated trace IDs showing two forked completion events for same session-key (trace ids: trc-6e8a, trc-6e8b). - Router debug: 2026-02-18T18:20:17Z routing decision showed parallel updates to route table for session-key prefix /s/lyceum/edu/ (see router.log lines attached in ticket). - Billing: usage bucket shows a spike between 18:22–18:48; raw token logs indicate duplicate write entries when both model variants reported token counts. Customer impact & ask: Lyceum is requesting a detailed RCA, confirmation of billing credit for duplicated tokens, and steps to prevent recurrence. They indicated this behavior affected live grading and transcript integrity during a scheduled assessment window. Priority: P0 due to session corruption and billing exposure.

investigation_notes: Concurrent canary-controller jobs were observed for two unrelated PRs; controller lacked leader-election per affinity prefix which allowed overlapping writes.
KV cache warmup raced with first request; when second variant accepted traffic before warmup completed both variants emitted completions leading to merged transcripts.
Streaming resets were caused by duplicate completion flush and immediate EOF from the second backend; GRPC stack did not surface clear differentiation between single-source EOF vs multi-source abort.
Token accounting double-counted when both variants reported token deltas in the same session window; billing dedupe assumed single-model reporting and missed parallel reports.
No evidence of client SDK issues; all reproductions used internal test harness that mirrored production session affinity behavior.
resolution: Root cause: race in canary-controller placement that allowed concurrent variant placement for identical session-affinity prefixes while KV caches were cold. Fixes implemented: 1) serialized placement per affinity prefix and leader election for controller jobs; 2) introduced 'kv-ready' handshake before routing traffic to a new variant; 3) GRPC streaming handling hardened to detect multi-backend completion and prefer single-source continuation; 4) Billing dedupe rule extended to include variant-id and session-window de-dup key to avoid double-charge during swaps. Rollout: hotfix deployed to us-east on 2026-02-20 and promoted globally on 2026-02-22. Customer remediation: billing credit issued (CM-2026-438210) and Lyceum notified; replayed and verified transcript integrity for impacted sessions. Follow-ups: update canary runbook to forbid parallel canary jobs touching overlapping affinity prefixes, add automated test for canary/kv warmup interactions, and schedule a joint runbook review with Lyceum on 2026-03-02.
